text.p: Ashland Inc said Thursday it continues to evaluate alternatives for its exploration division and its refining and marketing options.
The company also said it sees "several encouraging signs on the horizon."

Noting the previously announced filing of a registration statement for a proposed initial public offering of its exploration operations, now known as Blazer Energy Corp, the company said "The IPO is a viable option, but we also continue to evaluate other alternatives, including an outright sale, in an effort to produce the best value for our shareholders.
"In addition, we are continuing to aggressively review options for strategic alliances for our refining and marketing operations, but have nothing to announce at this time."

Ashland said it did not purchase any common shares during the quarter under a stock repurchase program approved by directors in December. The plan allows for the repurchase of up to one million Ashland common shares annually.
While second quarter, ended March 31, "financial results for the quarter were mixed, we see several encouraging signs on the horizon," Ashland said.
"APAC is poised for a strong year. Petroleum product margins have strengthened and our Midwest margins are currently above those on the Gulf Coast.

"If these conditions hold and with continued strength from our related energy and chemical operations, we are optimistic that the last half of 1997 will produce good profits for our shareholders." ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
